clue.text: Everybody at college too?

definitions.meaning: every body has a soul, so the whole company of souls stands for everyone
an Oxford college famous for its fellows-only membership

explanation.surface: A question whether the whole population is at university as well.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics on 'body' in the printed clue point to swapping body for soul: everybody becomes all souls. All Souls is an Oxford college with no undergraduates.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford foundation of that name is a college, and the phrase 'all souls' also means every person alive.

clue.text: An opening for bowmen or tax avoidance experts

definitions.text: An opening for bowmen or tax avoidance experts

parts.words: An opening for bowmen or tax avoidance experts
parts.note: a slit in a castle wall for archers to shoot through, and figuratively a gap in a law that clever accountants exploit

explanation.surface: A gap that suits both archers and accountants.
explanation.definitionFit: The word first meant a narrow slit in a fortification for shooting through, and now means an ambiguity used to evade a rule.

clue.text: Paris all right as a possible tonic

indicators.note: a possible version of the letters is a rearranged one

explanation.surface: Wondering if Paris, being fine, might be just the pick-me-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' rearranges PARIS ALL, R (right) and AS A into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The root drink was sold as a health-giving tonic and later as a soft drink.

clue.text: Fighters unfurled ?

parts.note: fighter aircraft spread out to protect ground forces form an overhead shield, like a rain shield opened up

explanation.surface: Combatants spreading out their banners.
explanation.walkthrough: Air cover by fighter planes is called an air umbrella; 'unfurled' fits the rain shield being opened.
explanation.definitionFit: A protective screen of fighter aircraft is called air cover, an overhead canopy like the rain shield opened.

clue.text: Direction to carry on packing

parts.note: S is south, a compass direction
taken as written
to wage war is to carry it on

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep going with filling the boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Stowage is the stowing away of cargo or goods, the packing of a hold.

clue.text: Wherein the evidence is negative ?

parts.note: evidence heard in private is heard 'in' this, and the device itself captures images on a photographic negative

explanation.surface: A question about where a trial's testimony proves nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A case heard 'in camera' is heard in private; the photographic device records its evidence on a negative.
explanation.definitionFit: The picture-taking device produces negatives, and court evidence given in private is given in camera.

clue.text: A case in the Tuileries

indicators.note: in shows the answer sits within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A box found in the famous Paris gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is thE TUIleries.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles or cosmetics.

clue.text: Forebodes a long time in the fourth estate

indicators.note: in puts the long time inside the fourth estate

parts.note: the press, journalists, are called the fourth estate
ages is a long time

explanation.surface: Someone foretelling a long stretch working in journalism.
explanation.definitionFit: To presage is to portend or foreshadow, so forebodes is the same verb form.

clue.text: He drives horses as an examiner-about a thousand

indicators.note: the examiner's word goes round the other pieces, as about can mean surrounding

parts.note: a tester is someone who examines or checks
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A carter who doubles as an inspector of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A and M (a thousand) inside TESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A teamster originally drove a team of draught animals such as horses.

clue.text: Square. How square ?

definitions.meaning: ...-square means solid and firm, foursquare honest
a square has this many sides and corners, and the number is itself a perfect square

explanation.surface: A geometry query asking what makes a square a square.
explanation.definitionFit: Four-square describes something steady and plain; and the count of a quadrilateral's sides answers 'how square?'.

clue.text: Fruit God doubtless could but didn't improve on

definitions.text: Fruit God doubtless could but didn't improve on

parts.words: Fruit God doubtless could but didn't improve on
parts.note: echoes the saying that doubtless God could have made a better berry, but doubtless God never did

explanation.surface: A tribute to a fruit so perfect even the Creator left it alone.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue alludes to William Butler's remark, quoted by Izaak Walton in The Compleat Angler, about a red summer berry.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation's berry is the red summer fruit eaten with cream at Wimbledon.

clue.text: She should be honest, .yet people get taken in by her

definitions.text: She should be honest, .yet people get taken in by her

parts.words: She should be honest, .yet people get taken in by her
parts.note: being taken in sounds like being fooled, but here visitors are received and shown in by the front-desk worker

explanation.surface: A woman who ought to be straight yet takes people in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests being deceived; at an office front desk it means being received and admitted.
explanation.definitionFit: The person at a front desk greets visitors and admits them, receiving them into the building.

clue.text: How glad these tidings, and how true !

definitions.text: How glad these tidings, and how true

parts.words: How glad these tidings, and how true
parts.note: glad tidings means good news, and something wholly true is called this kind of truth

explanation.surface: An exclamation of joy at news that is both happy and reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: The word's old English roots mean 'good news', and 'gospel truth' is the absolutely reliable kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian good news is the glad tidings, and indisputable fact is called gospel truth.

clue.text: Having a quick look at a grand college

parts.note: G is a common abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds
Lancing College is an English public school in Sussex

explanation.surface: Someone peering briefly at an impressive college building.
explanation.walkthrough: LANCING is a boarding school on the Sussex coast; the clue's 'college' points there rather than to a university.
explanation.definitionFit: To glance is to look briefly, so glancing is taking a quick look.

clue.text: Receives affirmative answer at second hand

parts.note: to hear news is to receive it
aye, also spelt ay, is an old word for yes

explanation.surface: Someone who gets a yes, but only passed on through another person.
explanation.definitionFit: Information known only from report, not first-hand witness, is hearsay.

clue.text: This pile's analysed ? So at least we hear

definitions.text: This pile's analysed ? So at least we hear

parts.words: This pile's analysed ? So at least we hear
parts.note: a pile here is a grand old building whose past has been studied and told, so we hear it described as famous in the past

explanation.surface: A question about a heap being examined, with the report as hearsay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pile' is a stately building, not a heap; one whose past is told and studied is what people call significant in history.
explanation.definitionFit: A building of note in the past is described as historic, and a grand old house is called a pile.

clue.text: Its points are named by boxers

definitions.text: Its points are named by boxers

parts.words: Its points are named by boxers
parts.note: sailors who 'box' the instrument recite its thirty-two points in order, so boxers here are not fighters

explanation.surface: A remark that pugilists name the points scored in a bout.
explanation.walkthrough: To box the compass is a sailor's term for reciting all its points in order; 'boxers' suggests the ring, and 'points' scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: The direction-finding instrument has points (north, north-by-east and so on) that sailors recite when boxing it.

clue.text: Mounted attendant, dismissed, has a problem

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
a rider is an extra problem following a geometry theorem

explanation.surface: A horseman, sacked, now has trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rider' in old maths textbooks was a supplementary problem set after a proposition.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrider is an escort riding on horseback beside a carriage.

clue.text: Tom's upset over censor's direction to players

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upwards, reading it backwards

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, so tom's gives cats
Cato the Elder was the Roman censor

explanation.surface: A man disturbed by the censor's instructions to actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the cats upwards in this down light, and 'over' places them above the censor. Cato the Elder, Roman censor, is the man meant; 'Tom' is a male cat, not a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato is a musical marking telling performers to play notes short and detached.

clue.text: Stuck, having split five hundred

parts.note: to cleave is to split
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Someone stuck after dividing a large sum.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb has two opposite senses: to split, and to adhere; the past form here means adhered.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave to something is to cling or adhere to it, so the past form means stuck.

clue.text: Altitude zero for a smooth voyage

definitions.meaning: heights are measured from the surface of the ocean
a calm, flat ocean gives an untroubled crossing

explanation.surface: A sailor's wish for flat water on the trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevations are reckoned from the mean ocean surface, and a flat, calm ocean is what a pleasant crossing needs.

clue.text: "Like a cloistress, she will —— walk" (T Night)

definitions.text: Like a cloistress, she will —— walk

parts.words: Like a cloistress, she will —— walk
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from Twelfth Night, where Olivia vows to walk covered like a nun

explanation.surface: A line from Twelfth Night with its missing word to supply.
explanation.walkthrough: In Twelfth Night (Act I, scene 1) Valentine reports that Olivia 'like a cloistress, she will veiled walk'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun traditionally wears a head covering, so she walks covered.

clue.text: 69 ways of constructing these lays (Kipling)

parts.note: Kipling wrote that there are nine and sixty ways of constructing a certain kind of lay, the songs of a people or clan

explanation.surface: A literary query about Kipling's line on the many ways of writing verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Kipling's 'In the Neolithic Age': 'There are nine and sixty ways of constructing tribal lays'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's quotation names the songs of a clan, verse belonging to a tribe.

clue.text: Music maker is getting into a mess in this set-up

parts.note: an organ is an instrument, a maker of music
taken as written

indicators.note: to make a mess of the words into a is to jumble their letters

explanation.surface: An instrument getting into a muddle within some institution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' signals that the letters of 'into a' are jumbled; 'getting' only joins. 'Music-maker' suggests a person, but it is the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An organisation is a structured body or arrangement, a set-up in the informal sense.

clue.text: Heavenly bodies in the gallery !

definitions.meaning: divine beings who dwell in heaven
the highest seats in a theatre are nicknamed for being nearest heaven

explanation.surface: Stars spotted in the theatre's top seats.
explanation.walkthrough: In British theatres the top gallery is called 'the gods'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deities are heavenly beings, and the cheap top tier of a theatre takes the same name.

clue.text: He makes'10 with a point

parts.note: the answer to 10 across is four, written IV in Roman numerals
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A player who reaches ten with one more point.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 10 across gives FOUR, here as the Roman numeral IV; 'He' defines a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan is a man's given name, the Russian form of John, so it can stand for 'he'.

clue.text: Native disturbance' that is ending

indicators.note: a disturbance stirs things up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A local uprising that is finally ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbance' rearranges IE and ENDING together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An indigene is a person born in a place, an aboriginal inhabitant.

clue.text: Temporal extent of the French allocation

parts.note: du is French for 'of the' before a masculine noun
a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: How long a French allowance lasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Duration is the length of time something lasts.
